content: FSRS vs SM-2: SM-2 tracks one ease factor per card, multiplies interval on success, resets on failure (causes 'low interval hell' on repeated failures). FSRS (open-spaced-repetition project) models per-card difficulty/stability/retrievability via a power-law forgetting curve, schedules review when predicted retrievability drops below a target (commonly 90%). FSRS-6 has 21 trainable parameters, defaults trained on ~700M reviews from ~10k Anki users; achieves same retention as SM-2 with ~20-30% fewer reviews. Optimizing personal FSRS parameters needs real review history: community guidance ranges from ~16 reviews (recent research floor) to official guidance of a few hundred to ~1000 reviews before optimization beats shipped defaults; below that you overfit noise. Default (population-trained) parameters are a reasonable starting point for a low-volume single-user dataset.
